theory.title: Testing Types & The Pyramid
theory.content:
The Testing Pyramid

The testing pyramid describes the ideal distribution of test types: many fast unit tests at the base, fewer integration tests in the middle, and a small number of end-to-end tests at the top.

  • Unit tests — test a single function or component in isolation. Fast (milliseconds), deterministic, easy to debug.
  • Integration tests — test how multiple units work together. May involve real databases, APIs, or file systems.
  • E2E tests — test a full user workflow in a real browser. Highest confidence, slowest, most expensive to maintain.

What to Test at Each Level

/* Unit — pure functions, component rendering */
test('formatDate returns MM/DD/YYYY', () => {
  expect(formatDate(new Date('2024-01-15'))).toBe('01/15/2024');
});

/* Integration — service + database */
test('createUser saves to DB and returns id', async () => {
  const user = await userService.create({ name: 'Alice' });
  expect(user.id).toBeDefined();
  const found = await db.users.findById(user.id);
  expect(found.name).toBe('Alice');
});

/* E2E — user action in browser */
test('user can sign in', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.fill('[name=email]', 'alice@example.com');
  await page.fill('[name=password]', 'secret');
  await page.click('[type=submit]');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
});

Static Analysis

TypeScript and ESLint catch entire classes of bugs before any test runs — they are the cheapest form of quality gate. Treat type errors and lint warnings as test failures in CI.

theory.title: Jest Fundamentals
theory.content:
Core API

Jest is a zero-config test runner with a rich assertion library. The key building blocks are describe, test/it, and expect.

describe('calculateTax', () => {
  test('returns 0 for zero income', () => {
    expect(calculateTax(0)).toBe(0);
  });

  test('applies 20% rate for standard income', () => {
    expect(calculateTax(1000)).toBeCloseTo(200);
  });

  test('throws for negative income', () => {
    expect(() => calculateTax(-1)).toThrow('Income cannot be negative');
  });
});

Matchers

  • toBe(val) — strict equality (===)
  • toEqual(val) — deep structural equality for objects/arrays
  • toContain(item) — array includes or string contains
  • toHaveBeenCalledWith(args) — mock was called with these arguments
  • toMatchSnapshot() — compare to stored snapshot

Lifecycle Hooks

beforeAll(async () => { await db.connect(); });   // once before the suite
afterAll(async () => { await db.disconnect(); });  // once after the suite
beforeEach(() => { store.reset(); });               // before each test
afterEach(() => { jest.clearAllMocks(); });         // after each test

Code Coverage

// package.json
"jest": {
  "collectCoverageFrom": ["src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
  "coverageThreshold": {
    "global": { "branches": 80, "functions": 90, "lines": 90 }
  }
}

// Run: npx jest --coverage

theory.title: Mocking Strategies
theory.content:
jest.fn() — Mock Functions

Creates a mock function that records all calls and can be configured to return specific values.

const mockFn = jest.fn();
mockFn.mockReturnValue(42);       // always returns 42
mockFn.mockResolvedValue({ ok: true }); // returns resolved Promise
mockFn.mockImplementation((x) => x * 2); // custom implementation

// Assertions
expect(mockFn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
expect(mockFn).toHaveBeenCalledWith('arg1', 'arg2');
expect(mockFn).toHaveReturnedWith(42);

jest.mock() — Module Mocking

// Auto-mock entire module (all exports become jest.fn())
jest.mock('./userService');

// Manual mock with implementation
jest.mock('./api', () => ({
  fetchUser: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({ id: 1, name: 'Alice' }),
  saveUser: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({ success: true }),
}));

// Import mocked module to configure in tests
import { fetchUser } from './api';
fetchUser.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('Network error'));

jest.spyOn() — Spies

Wraps an existing method to track calls while preserving the original implementation.

const spy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});

// Restore after test
spy.mockRestore();

Stubs vs Mocks vs Spies

  • Stub — replaces a function with a fixed response, no verification
  • Mock — like a stub but also verifies it was called correctly
  • Spy — wraps real function, observes calls without replacing behavior

theory.title: React Testing Library
theory.content:
Philosophy

React Testing Library (RTL) encourages testing components the way users interact with them — through the DOM — rather than testing implementation details like state or method calls.

Query Priority

Use the query that most closely mirrors how a real user (or assistive technology) would find the element:

  1. getByRole — most preferred; uses ARIA roles (button, heading, textbox)
  2. getByLabelText — for form inputs associated with a label
  3. getByPlaceholderText — less preferred; placeholder isn't a label
  4. getByText — for non-interactive visible text
  5. getByTestId — last resort; only when no semantic query is possible
import { render, screen, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';

test('submits the form', async () => {
  const user = userEvent.setup();
  const onSubmit = jest.fn();
  render();

  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'alice@example.com');
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText(/password/i), 'secret');
  await user.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }));

  expect(onSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
    email: 'alice@example.com',
    password: 'secret',
  });
});

Query Variants

  • getBy* — throws if not found (use for elements that should exist)
  • queryBy* — returns null if not found (use for absence assertions)
  • findBy* — async, waits up to timeout (use for async UI changes)

theory.title: Async Testing
theory.content:
Testing Promises with async/await

Always return or await Promises in tests. If you forget, the test completes before the assertion runs — giving a false positive.

test('fetchUser resolves with user data', async () => {
  const user = await fetchUser(1);
  expect(user.name).toBe('Alice');
});

test('fetchUser rejects on 404', async () => {
  await expect(fetchUser(999)).rejects.toThrow('User not found');
});

waitFor

Use waitFor to retry an assertion until it passes or the timeout is reached. Ideal for testing state changes that happen asynchronously.

test('shows loading then data', async () => {
  render();

  // Initially shows skeleton
  expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toBeInTheDocument();

  // Wait for the data to load
  await waitFor(() => {
    expect(screen.getByText('Alice')).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  // Skeleton gone
  expect(screen.queryByRole('status')).not.toBeInTheDocument();
});

findBy Queries

// findBy = waitFor + getBy in one call
const heading = await screen.findByRole('heading', { name: /dashboard/i });
expect(heading).toBeInTheDocument();

// With timeout option
const el = await screen.findByText('Loaded', {}, { timeout: 5000 });

MSW for API Mocking

import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';

const server = setupServer(
  http.get('/api/user/:id', ({ params }) => {
    return HttpResponse.json({ id: params.id, name: 'Alice' });
  })
);

beforeAll(() => server.listen());
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());

theory.title: E2E Testing with Playwright
theory.content:
Why Playwright

Playwright runs tests in real browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) with a modern async API. It has built-in auto-waiting, network interception, and powerful selectors.

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './e2e',
  use: {
    baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
  },
  projects: [
    { name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } },
    { name: 'mobile',   use: { ...devices['iPhone 12'] } },
  ],
});

Writing Tests

import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('user can complete checkout', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }).first().click();
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /cart/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /your cart/i })).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/checkout');
});

Page Object Model (POM)

class LoginPage {
  constructor(private page: Page) {}

  async login(email: string, password: string) {
    await this.page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill(email);
    await this.page.getByLabel(/password/i).fill(password);
    await this.page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  }
}

test('login works', async ({ page }) => {
  const loginPage = new LoginPage(page);
  await page.goto('/login');
  await loginPage.login('alice@example.com', 'secret');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
});

Best Practices

  • Prefer getByRole and getByLabel — they match accessibility semantics
  • Use data-testid sparingly, only when no semantic selector works
  • Keep E2E tests focused on critical user journeys — they are expensive
  • Use API setup (page.request) to seed data instead of clicking through setup flows

theory.title: Test Coverage & Best Practices
theory.content:
What Code Coverage Measures

Coverage reports how much of your source code is executed during tests. Four metrics:

  • Lines — percentage of executed lines
  • Branches — percentage of if/else/ternary paths taken
  • Functions — percentage of called functions
  • Statements — percentage of executed statements

100% coverage does NOT mean bug-free. Focus on branch coverage — it catches more logic errors than line coverage alone.

What to Test vs What to Skip

  • Test: business logic, edge cases, error paths, user-facing behavior
  • Skip: framework boilerplate, trivial getters, third-party library internals
  • Never test implementation details — tests that break when you refactor (without changing behavior) are a liability

Writing Maintainable Tests

// BAD — tests implementation detail (internal state)
test('sets isLoading to true', () => {
  const { result } = renderHook(() => useUsers());
  expect(result.current.isLoading).toBe(true); // fragile
});

// GOOD — tests observable behavior
test('shows spinner while loading', async () => {
  render();
  expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toBeInTheDocument();
  await waitFor(() => expect(screen.queryByRole('status')).not.toBeInTheDocument());
});

Test Organisation

  • Co-locate tests with source: Button.test.tsx next to Button.tsx
  • One describe block per component/function
  • Descriptive names: test('shows error message when email is invalid')
  • Arrange-Act-Assert pattern — keep each section clearly separated
